 SCCH-26 3 MVC 2932/2022  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Shaik Khadar Basha S/o.Shaik Moula @ S.Moula caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 06.05.2022 at about 10.40 pm., when the deceased Shaik Khada Basha was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BU-3654, when reached near Eidgapalle on Punganur-Madanapalle Road, at that time a Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-X-5994 which was wrongly parked by his driver without any indicator lights/signal in the middle of the road.
Due to this impact the rider of the motor cycle hit the lorry from behind which result in the accident.
As a result rider and pillion rider fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries and the pillion rider i.e., Shaik Khadar Basha succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital.
Due to the death of the deceased, the petitioners have put to untold misery and mental agony.
The petitioners i.e., father and minor sister were depending upon the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, deceased was working as Mechanic and cum Flower Decorator and he was earning monthly Rs.30,000/- per month.
The death was caused only due to the negligence of the driver of the first respondent.
The Punganur police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the lorry.
The 1 st respondent duly insured with the 2nd respondent, the policy was valid and was in force at the time of accident.
Therefore, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. After service of summons, both the respondents have appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statement separately.
5. Respondent No.1 has filed his written statement by contending that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent has denied the entire averments of the petition.

This respondent has admitted that he is the RC owner of the Lorry, bearing No. AP-02-X- 5994 and insured with the 2 nd respondent vide Policy No.1- 1YQX6POR P400-MK-500975 and valid from 22.07.2021 to 21.07.2022 and was in force as on the accident and the driver of the said vehicle was having valid driving license to drive the same and if any compensation is awarded then it has to be payable by the insurer of the vehicle only i.e., 2 nd respondent.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant and excessive.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
6. The Respondent No.2 has filed his written statement by contending that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 has denied the entire averments of the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of policy bearing No.MK500975 in respect of the Lorry,
bearing No.AP-02-X-5994 valid from 22.07.2021 to 21.07.2022 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It has contended that the rider of the motor cycle was riding the vehicle with high speed, without wearing helmet and also without possessing valid vehicle documents and dashed to rear right side portion of the insured vehicle, which was parked on extreme left side of the road without giving parking lights and also without taking any precautionary measures and the alleged accident occurred only due to his own negligence and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
The petition is bad for non joinder of proper and necessary parties.

Further contended that the petitioner is put to strict proof that the alleged driver of the insured vehicle and rider of the said motor cycle had valid and effective driving license to drive the class of vehicle at the time of alleged accident and respondent No.1 has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver, who was not possessing valid and effective driving license and thereby breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
7.
This respondent has also contended that, the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is needed to be a necessary party to the proceedings to adjudicate the matter fully and finally.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper party as the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is the necessary party to the proceedings.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party as such the rider and owner of the TP/motor cycle were not made as party to the proceedings.
It has not complied Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act 1988.
It has further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.

18. Learned counsel for respondent N.2 has submitted the written argument that as per statements of Sri.Kiran Kumar and Smt.Shantamma the deceased was riding the said motor cycle.

The alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the alleged deceased/rider of the said motor cycle,
who was riding the alleged motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BU-3654 in a rash and negligent manner with uncontrollable speed without wearing helmets and without knowledge of driving and dashed to the back side of the said lorry, which was parked on extreme left side of the road by putting indicators and taking all precautions to know the oncoming vehicles.
The alleged accident occurred in the Punganur Municipality Town.
As per sketch there are Electric Pole, Indian Bank ATM and other commercial shops near by the accident spot and the said lorry was parked at the extreme left side of the road.
It shows that there was sufficient light available at the accident spot and there is sufficient space towards right side for passing other vehicles.
Since the deceased/rider of the said motor cycle was riding the same negligently in uncontrollable speed, he could not notice the lorry even though there was sufficient light.
The insured vehicle was not at all responsible for the alleged accident and the alleged deceased had suffered the self accident by his own negligence.
The petitioners have not examined any eye witness to prove their claims.

It is specifically and emphatically denied that the alleged accident took place in the alleged manner as claimed by the petitioners, hence the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased/rider of the said motor cycle and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle and relied the following citations.

sentences.text: -Accident claim- Award- Insurance company Appeal-Plea of guilt by the driver- Conviction in the criminal case- Can the plea of guilt by the driver become the sole criterion for allowing the claim petition by the M.A.C.T- HELD, the M.A.C.T should not and ought not to place sole reliance on the judgment of the criminal court while considering the issue of the factum of the accident and the consequent negligence,as stated in the claim petition filed before the tribunal.
But, the Tribunal will have to access the evidence before it independently of any finding of the criminal court on the question of the driver pleading guilty.
At the most, the circumstance of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the parties of evidence to support the case of the claimant.

But, the Tribunal should not place implicit reliance only on the circumstance of the driver having pleaded guilty before the criminal court and as such an approach by the Tribunals will be not only an one sided approach but, at the same time, there is every likelihood of the pleading of guilty by a driver before the Criminal Court having been obtained by adopting various methods so as to ensure that the claimant succeeds before the M.A.C.T. in getting compensation.

- Further held,
There has been spate of cases wherein false claims have been made before the claims Tribunal and false implications are also on the increase.

The M.A.C.T.s are constituted not only to allow the claim petitions which are genuine in nature but, at the same time, the Tribunals also will have to keep in view that compensation should not be awarded mechanically in every case and to accept the case of the claimant as if all that the claimant says about the accident and the injuries is a truthful one.

Merely because a claimant in a particular case comes out with the evidence that the driver of the vehicle is convicted on his pleading guilty, the Tribunals should not go by the plead guilty factor alone, but it is required to appreciate the evidence before it from every angle and if there is a good reason to question the very case of the claimant or doubt the very manner of the accident, in such cases, the Tribunal will have to view the factor of pleading guilty along with the entire evidence before it and make an assessment of the whole situation.
19. The learned counsel for petitioners argued that the respondent No.2 has produced the statement of Cw-7 and CW-8, not produced the entire statements of witness.
The petitioners have produced the entire statements of the witnesses.
There is no question of contributory negligence of the deceased.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner.
In this regard the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on citations of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in - 2024 ACJ 2019 (SC) Radha Rani & Ors V/s Mohar Singh.

sentences.text: It is held that - Negligence - Contributory negligence - car dashed against a stationary truck resulting in death of car driver - Tribunal and High Court held that car driver was negligent to the extent of 20 per cent- truck was parked in the middle of road without any warning sign yet negligence has been attributed against car driver by observing that speed of car appeared to be extremely high and car driver could have avoided the accident; no material on record to substantiate such view; finding of contributory negligence of car driver set aside; award modified accordingly.

sentences.text: It is held that - Negligence - Contributory negligence - Leaving vehicle in a dangerous position -  Car dashed against a truck lying  unattended in the middle of highway without any indicators or parking lights causing death of three occupants of car and its driver and injury to one occupant - Tribunal and High Court found that accident could have been avoided had the car driver ben cautious and applying the rule of opportunity held that car driver was equally negligent in causing the accident -

Accident occurred during night and no evidence is forthcoming that road at the accident spot was well-lit therefore it would have been impossible for the incoming vehicles to sight the stationary truck within a reasonable distance -

Had the accident taken place during daytime or if the place of accident was well illuminated then car driver could have been held equally responsible for the accident by applying the rule of last opportunity- Truck was left abandoned in the middle of road in violation of rule 15 of Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 and no evidence is led to prove that leaving the truck in such position was beyond human control and that precautionary measures were taken while leaving the vehicle in that position-
No evidence that car was driven at excessively high speed or car driver did not follow traffic rules-Whether accident occurred due to sole negligence of truck driver."

Therefore, with due respect to the principle of above decisions relied by the petitioners, I am of the opinion that the facts of the present case is different from the facts of the decisions relied by the respondent No.2.
Hence, those decisions relied by the respondent No.2 are not helpful to the defence of the respondent No.2 and not applicable to this case.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-X-5994 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 and 2 in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.3:

As already discussed in Issue No.1, Petitioners are the father and sister of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
21. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:- PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased at Ex.P.8.
As per this document he was born on 01.12.1998.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was 24 years.
As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '18'.

sentences.text: It is stated that the deceased was working as a 'Mechanic cum Flower Decorator' and he was earning .30,000/- p.m.
In order to show the avocation and income of the deceased, in order to prove the same, Petitioners have not produced any document.
In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.

As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.15,500/- as the accident took place in the year 2022.
23.
As the deceased was 24 years as on the date of accident and same is considered as age of the deceased and proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
As the age of the deceased is below 40 years, 40% future prospects are to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the monthly income would be .15,500+6,200=.21,700/-.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, deceased was bachelor, hence 1/2 of the income to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and then the annual income would come around (21,700/- (-) 10,850/-) .10,850/-
x 12 = .1,30,200/- and by applying 18 multiplier,the loss of dependency would be .23,43,600/-.

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

As discussed supra that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of respondent No.1, who is the RC owner of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-X-5994 and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity in respect of the said lorry vehicle.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is owner of the offending lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-X-5994 and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was having valid insurance policy.

Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'Partly in the affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
 The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.24,20,600/- (Rupees  Twenty four lakh twenty thousand six hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Lorry is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.1 - 80%
 Petitioner No.2 - 20%

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 06.05.2022 at about 10.40 pm., when the deceased Shaik Khada Basha was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BU-3654, when reached near Eidgapalle on Punganur-Madanapalle Road, at that time a Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-X-5994 which was wrongly parked by his driver without any indicator lights/signal in the middle of the road.
9. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representative/heirs of deceased Shaik Khada Basha?
2. Whether the petitioners proves that, on 06.05.2022 at about 10.40 p.m., the deceased Shaik Khadar Basha was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BU-3654 and when they reached near Eigapalle, on Punganur- Madanapalle Road and at that time a lorry bearing No.AP-02-X-5994 was wrongly parked on the middle of the road without giving any signal or indicator, as a result the rider of the motor cycle dashed lorry from its behind and caused accident and thereby deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same while on the way to hospital, as mentioned in claim petition?
3. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
If so, from which respondent?
4. What Order or Award?

The death was caused only due to the negligence of the driver of the first respondent.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper party as the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is the necessary party to the proceedings.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party as such the rider and owner of the TP/motor cycle were not made as party to the proceedings.
It has not complied Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act 1988.
The learned counsel for petitioner has filed the following citations:
1) 2024 ACJ 2019 (SC) Radha Rani & Ors V/s Mohan Singh.
2) 2024 ACJ 2161 (SC) Sushma V/s Nitin Ganapati Rangole
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed the following citations:

2) MFA No.5896/2018 (Ms.Joyeeta Bose & Ors V/s Venkateshan.V & Ors)

The alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the alleged deceased/rider of the said motor cycle,
who was riding the alleged motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-BU-3654 in a rash and negligent manner with uncontrollable speed without wearing helmets and without knowledge of driving and dashed to the back side of the said lorry, which was parked on extreme left side of the road by putting indicators and taking all precautions to know the oncoming vehicles.
Since the deceased/rider of the said motor cycle was riding the same negligently in uncontrollable speed, he could not notice the lorry even though there was sufficient light.
The insured vehicle was not at all responsible for the alleged accident and the alleged deceased had suffered the self accident by his own negligence.
In this regard the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on citations of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in - 2024 ACJ 2019 (SC) Radha Rani & Ors V/s Mohar Singh.

At the most, the circumstance of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the parties of evidence to support the case of the claimant.
But, the Tribunal should not place implicit reliance only on the circumstance of the driver having pleaded guilty before the criminal court and as such an approach by the Tribunals will be not only an one sided approach but, at the same time, there is every likelihood of the pleading of guilty by a driver before the Criminal Court having been obtained by adopting various methods so as to ensure that the claimant succeeds before the M.A.C.T. in getting compensation.
The M.A.C.T.s are constituted not only to allow the claim petitions which are genuine in nature but, at the same time, the Tribunals also will have to keep in view that compensation should not be awarded mechanically in every case and to accept the case of the claimant as if all that the claimant says about the accident and the injuries is a truthful one.
Merely because a claimant in a particular case comes out with the evidence that the driver of the vehicle is convicted on his pleading guilty, the Tribunals should not go by the plead guilty factor alone, but it is required to appreciate the evidence before it from every angle and if there is a good reason to question the very case of the claimant or doubt the very manner of the accident, in such cases, the Tribunal will have to view the factor of pleading guilty along with the entire evidence before it and make an assessment of the whole situation.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.

-: ORDER :-
